correctness.rationale: Forcing k ordered pairwise disjoint boundary-cycle edges has exactly k! times (2n/(2n-k)) binomial(2n-k,k) possibilities and probability reciprocal to the relevant odd products. Forced adjacent chords have no crossings, so the remaining crossing distribution is exactly that of a uniformly matched 2(n-k)-point circle, establishing the mixed factorial identity for all finite n and all test functions. The first two factorial moments and established exact crossing moments yield the stated covariance and correlation. The bound E(S_n)_k <= 2^k allows dominated convergence of mixed transforms, and the published crossing CLT yields independent Gaussian/Poisson limits. Standalone enumeration of 3 through 10395 matchings verified 162 exact checks; this is corroboration, not an infinity certificate.

value.rationale: The existing random-chord literature states normal and Poisson marginals separately, which cannot settle their joint dependence. The exact mixed factorial polynomial identifies all finite-sample dependence between a local geometric statistic and global crossing statistic, proves nonzero negative correlation with the sharp dimensionless constant sqrt(5/(n+3)), and establishes their previously undetermined joint asymptotic independence. This is a natural complete classification of the marked-crossing statistic rather than an arbitrary numeric slice.
